record.one_liner: Open-source (MIT) Python command-line tool that checks whether a username exists across 400+ social networks and sites.
record.auth_notes: No API and no authentication. It is a local CLI that makes unauthenticated requests to the target sites. There are no vendor credentials.
record.access_notes: No hosted or public API. You install it yourself (pipx/pip/uv, Docker) and run it locally, which is free. The README does not mention a library API or a hosted service.
record.blocker: There is no API. A toolkit would have to run the CLI as a subprocess, which a community MCP server (Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp) already does with a single search_username tool. This needs a runtime that can execute the CLI. Results depend on the CLI's per-site checks, which can produce false positives and negatives. Searching people by username is a privacy and ToS consideration. By the strict definition (a hosted API with credentials) this is no_public_api; I rated it ready_with_caveats only because a local-CLI wrapper is feasible. Switch it to blocked if you require a hosted API.
